marketplace.article:
## Mail on a domain you control

Openship Mail combines SMTP, IMAP, mailbox administration, and webmail. Run your own mailboxes, or keep an existing provider and deploy the webmail client separately.

This entry opens the dedicated mail setup flow. Mail-server provisioning is available through desktop or self-hosted Openship; the Cloud mail console is not available yet.

## More than a web application

Mail needs a suitable host, mail DNS records, and reverse DNS alongside a working web address. Setup guides the server and domain configuration. The console manages accounts, certificates, and health afterwards.

Start with the [mail overview](/mail) and [mail API documentation](/docs/api/mail).

marketplace.article:
## A complete application backend

Supabase brings Postgres together with authentication, REST APIs, realtime updates, object storage, and Studio. It suits applications that need several backend capabilities in one stack.

The template declares the service stack and its API gateway. Generated configuration keeps shared credentials consistent, while Studio provides a browser interface for working with the backend.

## Plan for the full stack

Choose a destination with capacity for all services, review the install settings, and use the resulting API URL and application keys in your frontend or backend.

Set up backups for database records and stored files. Follow the [Supabase Docker self-hosting guide](https://supabase.com/docs/guides/self-hosting/docker) for additional integrations and operating guidance.

## A backend that stays in sync

Convex combines a database with application functions and reactive queries. Use it for applications where the interface needs to reflect changing data, from collaborative tools to live dashboards.

The Openship template runs the backend and developer dashboard together. The backend uses a persistent volume, and the catalog declares routes for its API, HTTP actions, and dashboard.

Open the dashboard and use the connection information from the install flow. Point your application and Convex tooling at the deployed backend, then deploy your functions using the upstream workflow.

Review the [Convex self-hosting guide](https://docs.convex.dev/self-hosting) for the operating model and supported setup.

marketplace.article:
## Object storage for your applications

MinIO provides an S3-compatible API for application uploads, media, exports, and other files that belong outside your relational database.

The template runs MinIO with persistent storage and a web console. Install settings configure the bucket, while generated credentials and connection details help you connect an application.

## Connect an S3 client

Use the endpoint and credentials from the connection card with your SDK or command-line client. Your client may need path-style addressing. The API endpoint and browser console use separate ports.

A persistent volume keeps files across container recreation; configure backups for important objects. The [community source repository](https://github.com/minio/minio) is archived. The template's actual image is listed below.

prepare.command: set -e; API=http://127.0.0.1:3000/api; J='Content-Type: application/json'; id1() { sed -n 's/.*"id":"\([^"]*\)".*/\1/p' | head -1; }; port1() { sed -n -e 's|.*"connection_string":"[^"]*@[^:"]*:\([0-9][0-9]*\)/.*|\1|p' -e 's/.*"port":\([0-9][0-9]*\).*/\1/p' | head -1; }; get() { curl -fsS -H "$A" "$1" 2>/dev/null || printf ''; }; post() { n=0; while [ $n -lt 20 ]; do r=$(curl -fsS -X POST "$1" -H "$J" -H "$A" -d "$2" 2>/dev/null || printf ''); [ -n "$r" ] && { printf %s "$r"; return 0; }; n=$((n+1)); sleep 2; done; printf ''; }; SETUP=$(curl -fsS "$API/auth/setup" || printf ''); case "$SETUP" in *'"registration_open":true'*) TOKEN=$(curl -fsS -X POST "$API/auth/register" -H "$J" -d "{\"name\":\"Admin\",\"email\":\"$ADMIN_EMAIL\",\"password\":\"$ADMIN_PASSWORD\"}" 2>/dev/null | sed -n 's/.*"token":"\([^"]*\)".*/\1/p') ;; *) TOKEN=$(curl -fsS -X POST "$API/auth/login" -H "$J" -d "{\"email\":\"$ADMIN_EMAIL\",\"password\":\"$ADMIN_PASSWORD\"}" 2>/dev/null | sed -n 's/.*"token":"\([^"]*\)".*/\1/p') ;; esac; [ -n "$TOKEN" ] || { echo "pg_port=no-token"; exit 0; }; A="Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"; ORG=$(get "$API/organizations" | id1); [ -n "$ORG" ] || ORG=$(post "$API/organizations" '{"name":"Default"}' | id1); [ -n "$ORG" ] || { echo "pg_port=no-org"; exit 0; }; P="$API/organizations/$ORG/projects"; PROJ=$(get "$P" | id1); [ -n "$PROJ" ] || PROJ=$(post "$P" '{"name":"main"}' | id1); [ -n "$PROJ" ] || { echo "pg_port=no-project"; exit 0; }; B="$P/$PROJ/branches"; BRJSON=$(get "$B"); BR=$(printf %s "$BRJSON" | id1); if [ -z "$BR" ]; then BR=$(post "$B" '{"name":"production"}' | id1); [ -n "$BR" ] || { echo "pg_port=branch-failed"; exit 0; }; curl -fsS -X PUT "$B/$BR/password" -H "$J" -H "$A" -d "{\"password\":\"$PG_PASSWORD\"}" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true; fi; PORT=$(printf %s "$BRJSON" | port1); [ -n "$PORT" ] || PORT=$(post "$B/$BR/endpoint" '' | port1); echo "pg_port=${PORT:-unstarted}"

firstLogin.note:
The admin account is created during install — use the email and password above. First boot initialises two embedded Postgres instances and can take a couple of minutes after a ~1.2 GB image pull.

Two things worth knowing, both upstream behaviour: if the console shows a branch as running but connections fail, stop and start that endpoint from the console — restarting the container can leave a stale compute lock behind while the API still reports it healthy. And if the container is killed hard (out of memory, power loss) it can refuse to boot with "lease already held"; delete neon_daemon_data/.lock inside the app's volume while nothing is running. An ordinary redeploy is safe — it shuts down gracefully and releases the lock.

marketplace.article:
## Postgres branches for development

This template packages self-hosted Neon through the community `neond` control plane. It provides branching, a browser console, and per-branch connection strings.

The community control plane bundles Neon's database components into one service. It is separate from Neon's proprietary hosted console. See the [neond source project](https://github.com/matisiekpl/neond) for its implementation.

## Understand the template's limits

The catalog describes this as a development and preview configuration. It has one container, no high-availability topology, a substantial image, and fixed host ports for branch endpoints.

Review those constraints and the template settings before choosing it for an important database workload.

<clickhouse>
  <!-- PostHog creates every table as ReplicatedMergeTree ON CLUSTER, so the
       macros, the clusters and ZooKeeper must all resolve or migrate_clickhouse
       cannot create a single table. Shipped as a config.d overlay rather than a
       replacement config.xml so the image's own defaults still apply. -->
  <zookeeper>
    <node>
      <host>zookeeper</host>
      <port>2181</port>
    </node>
  </zookeeper>
  <macros>
    <shard>01</shard>
    <replica>ch1</replica>
  </macros>
  <distributed_ddl>
    <path>/clickhouse/task_queue/ddl</path>
  </distributed_ddl>
  <!-- ~95 Kafka-engine tables each hold a background schedule slot. -->
  <background_schedule_pool_size>256</background_schedule_pool_size>
  <format_schema_path>/var/lib/clickhouse/format_schemas/</format_schema_path>
  <remote_servers>
    <posthog><shard><replica><host>clickhouse</host><port>9000</port></replica></shard></posthog>
    <posthog_single_shard><shard><replica><host>clickhouse</host><port>9000</port></replica></shard></posthog_single_shard>
    <posthog_migrations><shard><replica><host>clickhouse</host><port>9000</port></replica></shard></posthog_migrations>
    <posthog_writable><shard><replica><host>clickhouse</host><port>9000</port></replica></shard></posthog_writable>
    <posthog_primary_replica><shard><replica><host>clickhouse</host><port>9000</port></replica></shard></posthog_primary_replica>
    <ai_events><shard><replica><host>clickhouse</host><port>9000</port></replica></shard></ai_events>
    <aux><shard><replica><host>clickhouse</host><port>9000</port></replica></shard></aux>
    <ops><shard><replica><host>clickhouse</host><port>9000</port></replica></shard></ops>
    <sessions><shard><replica><host>clickhouse</host><port>9000</port></replica></shard></sessions>
  </remote_servers>
  <!-- PostHog's Kafka tables reference a named collection, not a broker list. -->
  <named_collections>
    <msk_cluster><kafka_broker_list from_env="KAFKA_HOSTS"/></msk_cluster>
    <warpstream_ingestion><kafka_broker_list from_env="KAFKA_HOSTS"/></warpstream_ingestion>
    <warpstream_calculated_events><kafka_broker_list from_env="KAFKA_HOSTS"/></warpstream_calculated_events>
    <warpstream_replay><kafka_broker_list from_env="KAFKA_HOSTS"/></warpstream_replay>
    <warpstream_shared><kafka_broker_list from_env="KAFKA_HOSTS"/></warpstream_shared>
    <warpstream_cyclotron><kafka_broker_list from_env="KAFKA_HOSTS"/></warpstream_cyclotron>
    <warpstream_logs><kafka_broker_list from_env="KAFKA_HOSTS"/></warpstream_logs>
    <warpstream_traces><kafka_broker_list from_env="KAFKA_HOSTS"/></warpstream_traces>
  </named_collections>
</clickhouse>

<clickhouse>
  <!-- CLICKHOUSE_SKIP_USER_SETUP=1 means the image creates no users, but the
       Django app connects as api/app/billing/dict_reader on different query
       paths. Passwords match the values the app is configured with; ClickHouse
       is never published outside the project network. -->

    <default>

      <profile>default</profile>

## A control plane for coding-agent runtimes

MindWire gives you one console for managing agents, credentials, and sessions while keeping the underlying runtime private.

The catalog defines the control plane and runtime together. The runtime stays behind the project network, and users enter through the console's public route.

build.dockerfile:
FROM alpine:3.24.1 AS downloader
ARG PB_VERSION=0.40.1
RUN apk add --no-cache ca-certificates unzip wget \
    && ARCH=$(uname -m) \
    && case "$ARCH" in x86_64) ARCH=amd64 ;; aarch64) ARCH=arm64 ;; *) echo "Unsupported architecture: $ARCH" >&2; exit 1 ;; esac \
    && wget -q https://github.com/pocketbase/pocketbase/releases/download/v${PB_VERSION}/checksums.txt -O /tmp/checksums.txt \
    && wget -q https://github.com/pocketbase/pocketbase/releases/download/v${PB_VERSION}/pocketbase_${PB_VERSION}_linux_${ARCH}.zip -O /tmp/pocketbase_${PB_VERSION}_linux_${ARCH}.zip \
    && cd /tmp \
    && grep " pocketbase_${PB_VERSION}_linux_${ARCH}.zip$" checksums.txt | sha256sum -c - \
    && unzip pocketbase_${PB_VERSION}_linux_${ARCH}.zip -d /pb
FROM alpine:3.24.1
RUN apk add --no-cache ca-certificates su-exec \
    && addgroup -S pocketbase \
    && adduser -S -G pocketbase -h /pb pocketbase
COPY --chown=pocketbase:pocketbase --from=downloader /pb/pocketbase /pb/pocketbase
COPY --chown=pocketbase:pocketbase pocketbase/entrypoint.sh /pb/entrypoint.sh
RUN chmod 755 /pb/entrypoint.sh
WORKDIR /pb
ENTRYPOINT ["/pb/entrypoint.sh"]
CMD ["/pb/pocketbase", "serve", "--http=0.0.0.0:8090", "--encryptionEnv=PB_ENCRYPTION_KEY"]

files.content:
#!/bin/sh
set -eu
mkdir -p /pb/pb_data
chown pocketbase:pocketbase /pb/pb_data
export PB_ENCRYPTION_KEY="$(printf '%.32s' "$PB_ENCRYPTION_SEED")"
if [ ! -e /pb/pb_data/.openship-superuser ]; then
  su-exec pocketbase /pb/pocketbase superuser upsert "$POCKETBASE_SUPERUSER_EMAIL" "$POCKETBASE_SUPERUSER_PASSWORD" --dir=/pb/pb_data --encryptionEnv=PB_ENCRYPTION_KEY >/dev/null
  su-exec pocketbase touch /pb/pb_data/.openship-superuser
fi
exec su-exec pocketbase "$@"

files.content:
import configparser
import os
import subprocess
import time
from pathlib import Path
import psycopg2

env = os.environ
deadline = time.monotonic() + 120
while True:
    try:
        connection = psycopg2.connect(host=env['HOST'], user=env['USER'], password=env['PASSWORD'], dbname='postgres', connect_timeout=5)
        break
    except psycopg2.OperationalError:
        if time.monotonic() >= deadline:
            raise RuntimeError('PostgreSQL did not become ready') from None
        time.sleep(2)
with connection, connection.cursor() as cursor:
    cursor.execute('SELECT 1 FROM pg_database WHERE datname = %s', ('odoo',))
    exists = cursor.fetchone() is not None
connection.close()
config = configparser.ConfigParser(interpolation=None)
config['options'] = {'admin_passwd': env['OPENSHIP_MASTER_PASSWORD'], 'data_dir': '/var/lib/odoo', 'addons_path': '/mnt/extra-addons', 'db_host': env['HOST'], 'db_user': env['USER'], 'db_password': env['PASSWORD'], 'db_port': '5432'}
path = '/var/lib/odoo/openship.conf'
with open(path, 'w') as file:
    os.chmod(path, 0o600)
    config.write(file)
if not exists:
    result = subprocess.run(['odoo', 'db', '--config', path, 'init', 'odoo', '--username', env['OPENSHIP_ADMIN_EMAIL'], '--password', env['OPENSHIP_ADMIN_PASSWORD']])
    if result.returncode:
        raise RuntimeError('Odoo database initialization failed; existing data has been preserved')
# Never delete, recreate, or reset credentials in an existing database.
os.execvp('odoo', ['odoo', '--config', path, '--database=odoo', '--db-filter=^odoo$', '--no-database-list', '--proxy-mode'])

#!/bin/sh
set -eu
# The official image's init-only entry point installs files and wp-config.php.
# Apache starts only after the generated owner account exists.
docker-ensure-installed.sh
attempt=0
until php -r 'mysqli_report(MYSQLI_REPORT_OFF); $db = @new mysqli(getenv("WORDPRESS_DB_HOST"), getenv("WORDPRESS_DB_USER"), getenv("WORDPRESS_DB_PASSWORD"), getenv("WORDPRESS_DB_NAME")); exit($db->connect_errno ? 1 : 0);'; do
  attempt=$((attempt + 1))
  [ "$attempt" -lt 60 ] || exit 1
  sleep 2
done
su -s /bin/sh www-data -c 'wp core is-installed' || su -s /bin/sh www-data -c 'wp core install --url="$OPENSHIP_PUBLIC_URL" --title="$OPENSHIP_SITE_TITLE" --admin_user="$OPENSHIP_ADMIN_USER" --admin_password="$OPENSHIP_ADMIN_PASSWORD" --admin_email="$OPENSHIP_ADMIN_EMAIL" --skip-email'
